newsitem.title: UK: Beach, not sandbox, ideal for sandcastles.
newsitem.headline: Beach, not sandbox, ideal for sandcastles.

text.p: Beach sand is better for building sandcastles than the sand found in children's playgrounds and scientists said on Wednesday they had now found out why.
Wet sand, they said, sticks together better than dry sand and tiny drops of water stay in between the grains of sand even after the castle appears to have dried out.

Peter Schiffer and colleagues at Notre Dame University examined the physics of sand castles and found, to their surprise, that extremely tiny amounts of water were enough to keep the grains of sand sticking together.
That is why a sand castle still stands even after it appears to have dried out, they wrote in a letter to the science journal Nature.
They said their findings could have implications for engineers working with concrete, agriculture and even the manufacture of tablets.
